newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset attacks Enel phone bid.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset attacks Enel phone bid.

text.p: Italian electricity utility Enel is a real monopoly and as such cannot take on the role of a mobile phone operator, said Fedele Confalonieri, chairman of multi-media group Mediaset.
ENEL plans to launch a joint bid with Germany's Deutsche Telekom for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence. The government is expected to invite bids this month.
Mediaset will also be bidding with energy giant ENI, in partnership with British Telecom and Italian bank BNL in the Albacom joint venture.

"I believe Enel to be really monopolistic...because it is alone in supplying electricity to millions of households, and so uses the resources deriving from this monopoly to compete with others in other sectors," Confalonieri told reporters while attending a business meeting.
He said it was questionable whether Enel should act in this way, "but if at the end of the day the controlling bodies allow it to do so, we can't do anything about it."
"We are ready to bid for the third operating licence, we've been working on the project with ENI for six months," he said.
Italy currently has two mobile phone service operators, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Olivetti- controlled Omnitel.
Olivetti last week complained of "dangerous interference" that could be caused by the bid led by Enel.

Olivetti's chief executive Roberto Colaninno told Milan's Corriere della Sera newspaper that Omnitel was already competing with one state-controlled operator, TIM, and that the new bid if successful could see two state operators in the field.
"The entry of Enel into the market constitutes a serious distortion of competition in the market," he told the paper.
